change: New open-data benchmark for the four concrete generators: cylinders and notched beams D = 93 and 215 mm from Hoover et al. (2013), one batch with f_c = 55.6 MPa, cards generated from f_c and d_max only. All four reproduce the measured size effect within 4 %; peak loads are −21 % (KCC), +7 to +15 % (Winfrith, CSCM, CDP). The fib MC2010 G_F used by the KCC and CDP generators is 35–55 % above this concrete's measured G_F, and CDP dissipates exactly its card value.

New fracture model input (default 1 = GISSMO): with Z given, the generator writes *MAT_ADD_DAMAGE_GISSMO with a Rice–Tracey failure curve ε_f(η) = ε₀ exp(−1.5(η − 1/3)), ε₀ = kG(1 mm) · ln(1/(1−Z)), an LCREGD element-size curve kG(h)/kG(1 mm), ECRIT = plastic strain at A_g, DMGEXP = 2 and FADEXP = 4. kG = 1.63, 1.37, 1.21 and 0.91 for h = 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 3 mm, calibrated on the BAM S355 flat specimen. One card breaks the specimen at A = 34.0–35.4 % on all four meshes, with a gradual load drop. Fracture model 0 keeps the FAIL output of version 1.2. Unit conversion now also rescales the element-size axis of LCREGD.
New example: the S355 flat specimen with the generator's GISSMO card on four meshes, against the BAM tests and the FAIL run.

Beyond A_g the curve now continues with slope H = σ_true(A_g) (Considère slope) instead of a flat tail, so the neck starts at A_g and grows gradually. New optional ductile fracture: FAIL = k(h) · ln(1/(1−Z)) from the reduction of area Z and the element size h, with k = 1.29, 1.13, 1.02 and 0.81 for h = 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 3 mm. Calibrated on BAM S355 flat tensile tests: the specimen breaks at A = 34.8–35.1 % (test 35 %) on every mesh.

New example: S355 flat specimen pulled to fracture, compared with three BAM tensile tests (Zenodo 6778336). The round-bar example was rerun with the new MAT_024 curve, with and without FAIL. Cylinder example: Winfrith's rise to 42 MPa after the peak traced to hourglass forces (two extra runs with IHQ 6 and IHQ 1 give 35 MPa and collapse); the card is not the cause.

Documentation: RATE also sets the meaning of FE. With RATE = 1 (generator) FE is the crack width wc; with RATE = 0 it is the fracture energy G_F, scaled with strength by the rate factor. Checked by single-element tension in LS-DYNA R13: RATE = 1 dissipates ½·UTS·FE within 0.5 % for 10 and 20 mm elements.

New output-unit selector: mm·ms·g·N·MPa (default), mm·ms·kg·kN·GPa, mm·s·t·N·MPa, SI m·s·kg·N·Pa, cm·µs·g·Mbar and in·s·lbf·psi. Inputs stay in mm, ms, g, N, MPa; every field of the card is rescaled by its dimension, including Winfrith CONM, KCC RSIZE/UCF and the CSCM rate parameters ETA0C/ETA0T (time^(1−n)). Checked with single-element tension and compression runs in LS-DYNA R13: the same stresses in all systems (within 0.3 % at peak).

Fracture energy is now regularised to the element-size input: λ6–λ10 are stretched so that one cracked element dissipates G_F (fib MC2010 by default, or the new optional G_F input). Checked by single-element tension in LS-DYNA R13: within 2.5 % of the target for h = 5–50 mm and f_c = 20–60 MPa. The compressive peak is unchanged.

f_c is now treated as the measured mean cylinder strength: the modulus no longer adds 8 MPa twice (E was computed from f_c + 16) and G_F uses f_c directly. GFT/GFS are written with 5 decimals (0.0753 was written as 0.08). ETA0C/ETA0T converted from s to ms and ETA0T now uses f_c in psi; both match *MAT_CSCM_CONCRETE in LS-DYNA R13. New IRATE input (default 0).
FT now follows EN 1992-1-1 with f_c as the mean cylinder strength: fctm = 0.30 (f_c − 8)^(2/3) (2.35 MPa at f_c = 30 MPa, was 2.90).
f_c is now the mean cylinder strength (fcm = f_c, no longer f_c + 8): TM and GFt use f_c, UTS = 0.30 (f_c − 8)^(2/3) per EN 1992-1-1.

RSIZE is now 1/25.4 = 3.937E-2 (was 3.972E-2). Documentation adds single-element tension tests showing that the dissipated fracture energy scales with element size below LOCWID (0.05 N/mm at 5 mm, 0.26 N/mm at 25 mm for f_c = 30 MPa).
Cards 3 and 4 (EPS1–8, ES1–8) are now written. LS-DYNA requires them even when LCSS is used; without them the deck stopped with an input error. Checked in an LS-DYNA R13 tensile-bar run.

New inputs: dif_model (0 = rate effects off, 1 = CEB-FIP MC90 + Malvar & Ross, 2 = fib MC2010) and rate_cap (DIF held constant above it, default 300 1/s, as in the manual's sample curve). Checked in LS-DYNA R13: peak/f_c = 0.998, 1.270 and 1.156 at 1 1/s.

Rewrote the generator to the R13 card layout (MID RO G E PR / A B N C M TM TR EPS0 / CP PC SPALL IT D1–D4 / D5 EROD EFMIN NUMINT) with 10-column fields. Adds G, the *EOS_LINEAR_POLYNOMIAL required for solids, EPS0 converted from 1/s to 1/ms, CP, PC and optional D1–D5. Checked against the analytical JC curve in a single-element LS-DYNA R13 test.

Rewrote the generator to the R13 card layout (MID RO PR A B REF / SGL SW ST LCID). Removed the K input, which is not a MAT_027 field; PR now limited to 0.49–0.4999 as the manual recommends. Checked against the analytical uniaxial response in LS-DYNA R13.

BETA labels corrected (0 = kinematic, 1 = isotropic, per the manual). FS is now written blank when not given (LS-DYNA default: no erosion); FS = 0 behaved the same in R13. SRC hint now states 1/ms units.
Theory notes converted from PDF to a page, with the formulas the generator uses.

DIF curve abscissa converted from 1/s to 1/ms (the model runs in ms; rate effects were shifted by a factor of 1000). Compressive DIF now switches to the steep CEB-FIP branch at 30 1/s instead of 1e5. *EOS_TABULATED_COMPACTION written with 16-character fields; LS-DYNA could not read the EOS before. Matches the manual's 45.4 MPa sample curve; checked in LS-DYNA R13. Theory notes added.
